text.f: The dragon has scorched its tax receipts. Its accountant is hiding in a biscuit tin and refuses to come out until you sort them.
text.c: The accountant has taken shelter in a biscuit tin. Apparently, the dragon considers breathing fire at the paperwork a valid filing system.
text.x: The dragon has burned its own tax receipts. Its accountant is hiding in a biscuit tin, and the bastard has left you to sort it out.

choices.label: Sort the scorched receipts
choices.win: You recover the figures. The accountant gives you a folder marked STRICTLY LESS FLAMMABLE.
choices.lose: You mistake three important receipts for crumbs and sweep them away.

onWin.memory: You recover the figures. The accountant gives you a folder marked STRICTLY LESS FLAMMABLE.

choices.label: Buy the accountant's emergency duplicate
choices.win: You collect the emergency duplicate from beneath the biscuits.
choices.lose: The accountant refuses to open the tin.

onWin.memory: You collect the emergency duplicate from beneath the biscuits.

choices.label: Carry the receipts to the tax office
choices.win: You deliver the entire stack. The clerk asks why you did not use a folder.
choices.lose: The stack topples into a brazier. The accountant starts packing.

onWin.memory: You deliver the entire stack. The clerk asks why you did not use a folder.

onLose.memory: The stack topples into a brazier. The accountant starts packing.

text.f: The receipts include a claim for repairing a village the dragon burned. The auditor says damage you caused yourself is not a business expense.
text.c: The dragon has claimed replacement roofs as a business expense. The auditor asks why every invoice mentions the same dragon-shaped hole.
text.x: The dragon wants a tax deduction for rebuilding the village it burned down. The auditor says being a destructive bastard is not a profession.

choices.label: Reclassify the village as dependent relatives
choices.win: The auditor accepts the villagers as dependants. The dragon now owes them birthday presents.
choices.lose: The villagers demand pocket money. The dragon takes its frustration out on you.

onWin.memory: The auditor accepts the villagers as dependants. The dragon now owes them birthday presents.

choices.label: Ask the dragon to pay for the roofs
choices.win: The dragon agrees to compensate the villagers. The auditor accepts the corrected return.
choices.lose: The dragon calls the villagers ungrateful. A roof tile flies through the window.

onWin.memory: The dragon agrees to compensate the villagers. The auditor accepts the corrected return.

text.f: The receipts are gone. The auditor wants another record of the dragon's expenses. A knight arrives with an itemised bill for scorched armor.
text.c: The auditor needs proof of expenses. Fortunately, the dragon's last visitor has kept every bill for repairing his armor. He has kept a grudge, too.
text.x: No receipts. A knight arrives with a repair bill and a grudge. For once, the dragon's habit of setting people on fire might solve the bloody paperwork.

choices.label: Value the damage to the knight’s armor
choices.win: You verify the repair costs. The knight gets compensation and the dragon gets an accurate bill.
choices.lose: You underestimate the repairs. The knight demonstrates the dent using your helmet.

onWin.memory: You verify the repair costs. The knight gets compensation and the dragon gets an accurate bill.

onLose.memory: You underestimate the repairs. The knight demonstrates the dent using your helmet.

choices.label: Shield the knight from another blast
choices.win: You protect the witness. The auditor adds a fireproof screen to the approved expenses.
choices.lose: The dragon scorches you as well. The auditor requests another repair estimate.

onWin.memory: You protect the witness. The auditor adds a fireproof screen to the approved expenses.

finaleChoices.label: Submit the fireproof duplicate with everything itemised
finaleChoices.win: Every deduction has a receipt. The dragon gets a refund and buys the accountant a larger tin.
finaleChoices.lose: The refund is approved in copper. Delivery crushes the desk.

onWin.memory: The fireproof duplicate won the dragon a tax refund.

text.f: The lich answers the door in slippers. His lease is nine hundred years old, but the clause about returning his deposit is perfectly clear.
text.c: The lich has ignored nine centuries of rent increases. He has, however, calculated every penny of interest owed on his deposit.
text.x: The lich has lived rent-free for nine hundred years. Now the old bastard wants his deposit back, with interest.

choices.label: Read the nine-hundred-year break clause
choices.win: The lease allows eviction once the deposit is returned. You finally have terms to negotiate.
choices.lose: The lich reads the entire lease aloud. He pokes you with his staff whenever you doze off.

onWin.memory: The lease allows eviction once the deposit is returned. You finally have terms to negotiate.

choices.label: Pay for a specialist moving van
choices.win: The movers agree to carry the lich, his coffin and all his jars.
choices.lose: The movers refuse the booking.

onWin.memory: The movers agree to carry the lich, his coffin and all his jars.

choices.label: Take the front door off its hinges
choices.win: The lich agrees to discuss moving before you dismantle anything else.
choices.lose: The door falls on you. The lich adds it to the damages claim.

onLose.memory: The door falls on you. The lich adds it to the damages claim.

text.f: The lich will leave if you find a home for him and his undead goldfish. The new landlord wants a pet reference. The fish has outlived six landlords.
text.c: You find a flat, but the landlord wants a reference for the lich's undead goldfish. Its previous owners are unavailable for comment.
text.x: The new landlord wants a pet reference for the lich's undead goldfish. Nine hundred years in a bowl, and the poor sod still needs a character witness.

choices.label: Write the goldfish a good reference
choices.win: The landlord approves the fish. The lich starts packing his coffin.
choices.lose: The landlord phones a previous neighbor. The fish has a noise complaint.

onWin.memory: The landlord approves the fish. The lich starts packing his coffin.

choices.label: Teach the goldfish to play dead
choices.win: The fish keeps still during the inspection. The landlord approves an apparently empty bowl.
choices.lose: The fish performs a vigorous resurrection halfway through the inspection. The landlord throws you out.

onWin.memory: The fish keeps still during the inspection. The landlord approves an apparently empty bowl.

text.f: The lich has packed his soul in a jam jar. Unfortunately, it is identical to thirty jars of marmalade. He refuses to move until you find it.
text.c: Thirty-one jars, thirty labels saying MARMALADE. One contains an immortal soul. The lich admits his filing system could use work.
text.x: The lich keeps his soul beside the marmalade. Every jar has the same bloody label, and he refuses to leave without the right one.

choices.label: Find the jar that whispers threats
choices.win: You identify the soul jar by its threats against the landlord.
choices.lose: You open the wrong jar. The soul jar rolls off the shelf and hits your foot.

onWin.memory: You identify the soul jar by its threats against the landlord.

choices.label: Carry every jar to the moving van
choices.win: You move the whole collection. The lich promises to label it before his next eviction.
choices.lose: The crate slips. You catch the soul jar with your knee.

onWin.memory: You move the whole collection. The lich promises to label it before his next eviction.

text.f: The king's left sock has run away. A talking laundry basket saw it board a train, but wants protection from the royal washerwoman before it gives evidence.
text.c: The laundry basket saw the sock board a train. It will talk if you can guarantee it never has to hold the king's underwear again.
text.x: The laundry basket knows where the sock went. It wants witness protection, which seems fair after years of holding the king's filthy pants.

choices.label: Offer the basket a new job
choices.win: The basket agrees to become a bread bin and gives you the sock’s destination.
choices.lose: The washerwoman overhears and throws a wet towel at you.

onWin.memory: The basket agrees to become a bread bin and gives you the sock’s destination.

choices.label: Buy the sock’s train records
choices.win: The ticket office confirms the sock travelled to the textile workers’ hall.
choices.lose: The ticket office refuses to release the records.

onWin.memory: The ticket office confirms the sock travelled to the textile workers’ hall.

choices.label: Search the king’s drawer for clues
choices.win: You find a union leaflet and a very small railway timetable.
choices.lose: The drawer sticks. When you pull harder, it lands on your foot.

onLose.memory: The drawer sticks. When you pull harder, it lands on your foot.

text.f: You find the sock at a union meeting. It wants shorter working hours and a king who washes his feet. A left glove takes the minutes.
text.c: The runaway sock has formed a union. Its demands are a five-day week, regular washing and an end to being called 'the spare one'.
text.x: The sock wants a five-day week and a king who washes his bloody feet. The left glove taking the minutes says these are modest demands.

choices.label: Draft a five-day footwear week
choices.win: The sock agrees to return if the king signs the contract.
choices.lose: The glove spots a loophole. The sock’s supporters pelt you with pegs.

onWin.memory: The sock agrees to return if the king signs the contract.

choices.label: Hear the sock out
choices.win: The sock explains its grievances. You persuade it to attend a meeting with the king.
choices.lose: You call it an odd sock. Its supporters take exception to that.

onWin.memory: The sock explains its grievances. You persuade it to attend a meeting with the king.

text.f: The royal tailor has knitted a replacement sock to hide the disappearance. It is green, lumpy and plainly the wrong size. He begs you not to tell the king.
text.c: The tailor's replacement sock looks like a turnip. He calls it an experimental fit. The king is due to inspect it in five minutes.
text.x: The tailor has knitted something resembling a turnip and called it a sock. He wants your help selling this obvious cock-up to the king.

choices.label: Distract the king during the fitting
choices.win: You keep the king talking while the tailor hides the replacement.
choices.lose: The king looks down, sees the lump and demands an explanation. The tailor points at you.

onWin.memory: You keep the king talking while the tailor hides the replacement.

choices.label: Follow the thread to the tailor’s workshop
choices.win: You find the original sock’s union leaflet beside the knitting needles.
choices.lose: You pull the wrong thread and bring a shelf of wool down on your head.

onWin.memory: You find the original sock’s union leaflet beside the knitting needles.

finaleChoices.label: Offer the sock its negotiated footwear contract
finaleChoices.win: The sock returns on union terms. The king must now wash his own feet.
finaleChoices.lose: The king signs with his right hand. Talks briefly collapse.

onWin.memory: The king accepted union terms for his left sock.

text.f: Both armies have stopped you at the checkpoint. The customer is across the battlefield. Each commander insists you must use the other side's delivery gate.
text.c: Two armies, two checkpoints, no agreed delivery route. The sandwich is getting cold while the commanders argue about which side ordered mustard.
text.x: The commanders are arguing about which gate you can use. The sandwich is going cold, and neither bastard is willing to admit they could just let you through.

choices.label: Declare the sandwich neutral
choices.win: Both commanders accept a neutral lunch delivery. You get a pass for the battlefield.
choices.lose: One commander calls it enemy catering and has you removed from the checkpoint.

onWin.memory: Both commanders accept a neutral lunch delivery. You get a pass for the battlefield.

choices.label: Pay for an escorted delivery route
choices.win: The guards open a protected route across the battlefield.
choices.lose: The guards refuse to open the gate.

onWin.memory: The guards open a protected route across the battlefield.

choices.label: Sprint between the catapults
choices.win: You reach the far checkpoint with the sandwich still wrapped.
choices.lose: You dodge a stone and land on the sandwich. The customer will notice.

onWin.memory: You reach the far checkpoint with the sandwich still wrapped.

onLose.memory: You dodge a stone and land on the sandwich. The customer will notice.

text.f: Today's soup introduces itself as Gregory. It wants to leave the restaurant before lunch. The waiter approaches with a bowl and an encouraging smile.
text.c: The soup's name is Gregory. He would like to be taken off the menu, preferably before the waiter finishes recommending him.
text.x: Gregory the soup would rather not be lunch. The waiter calls him today's special. Gregory calls the waiter a heartless bastard.

choices.label: Disguise Gregory as a table decoration
choices.win: You float flowers in the bowl. The waiter mistakes Gregory for a centerpiece.
choices.lose: Gregory sneezes pepper over the waiter. The disguise is ruined.

onWin.memory: You float flowers in the bowl. The waiter mistakes Gregory for a centerpiece.

choices.label: Buy Gregory as a takeaway
choices.win: You buy the whole bowl. Gregory asks you to keep the receipt in case freedom needs proof of purchase.
choices.lose: The waiter refuses the takeaway order.

onWin.memory: You buy the whole bowl. Gregory asks you to keep the receipt in case freedom needs proof of purchase.

choices.label: Carry Gregory’s table outside
choices.win: You lift the table and head for the door. The waiter assumes you have booked a private function.
choices.lose: The table catches in the doorway. Hot soup splashes your hands.

onWin.memory: You lift the table and head for the door. The waiter assumes you have booked a private function.

text.f: At the door, Gregory asks you to rescue the garlic bread as well. He calls it his uncle. The chef says family discounts do not apply to the menu.
text.c: Gregory will not leave without the garlic bread he calls Uncle. The chef says it comes with the soup only if you pay for the meal deal.
text.x: Gregory insists the garlic bread is his uncle. The chef wants another three gold. Rescuing an entire bloody meal is becoming expensive.

choices.label: Smuggle the garlic bread in your sleeve
choices.win: You slip the bread into your sleeve. Gregory thanks you for saving Uncle.
choices.lose: The hot bread burns your arm. You drop it and attract the chef’s attention.

onWin.memory: You slip the bread into your sleeve. Gregory thanks you for saving Uncle.

choices.label: Persuade Gregory to leave without it
choices.win: Gregory agrees to send someone back for the bread. For now, getting out alive takes priority.
choices.lose: Gregory shouts for Uncle. The chef hears and reaches for his ladle.

onWin.memory: Gregory agrees to send someone back for the bread. For now, getting out alive takes priority.

text.f: The chef blocks the kitchen exit. Gregory tries to stay quiet, but every time the chef reaches for a spoon he screams. You need a distraction.
text.c: Gregory's disguise has failed. He shouted 'I am ordinary soup' at the chef, who is now standing between you and the exit.
text.x: The chef has caught you. Gregory keeps shouting that he is ordinary soup, which is a bloody terrible way to prove it.

choices.label: Pretend to be a kitchen inspector
choices.win: The chef hides his dirty pans. You carry Gregory out while he is busy.
choices.lose: The chef asks for identification. Your improvised badge fails to impress him.

onWin.memory: The chef hides his dirty pans. You carry Gregory out while he is busy.

choices.label: Taste the decoy soup and keep talking
choices.win: You keep the chef occupied with a detailed review while Gregory edges towards the door.
choices.lose: The decoy soup is scalding. Your yelp brings the chef straight back.

onLose.memory: The decoy soup is scalding. Your yelp brings the chef straight back.

text.f: The goblins want helmets, lunch breaks and dental care. The dark lord says helmets are cheaper. He has not noticed their list includes a ban on compulsory headbutts.
text.c: The goblins want dental care. The dark lord offers helmets and asks them to headbutt more carefully. Negotiations have stalled.
text.x: The dark lord refuses dental care and suggests the goblins stop breaking their teeth. He is also the bastard making them headbutt castle gates.

choices.label: Explain why dental care costs less
choices.win: You show the dark lord the replacement-helmet bills. He agrees to discuss dental care.
choices.lose: He orders a practical demonstration. You are handed a helmet and shown a wall.

onWin.memory: You show the dark lord the replacement-helmet bills. He agrees to discuss dental care.

choices.label: Donate to the strike fund
choices.win: The goblins can afford to keep striking. They ask you to speak for them.
choices.lose: The strike fund refuses the donation.

onWin.memory: The goblins can afford to keep striking. They ask you to speak for them.

choices.label: Demonstrate a safer way to break gates
choices.win: You use a battering ram. Several goblins ask why nobody mentioned these before.
choices.lose: The ram swings backwards and knocks you off the platform.

onWin.memory: You use a battering ram. Several goblins ask why nobody mentioned these before.

text.f: The goblins ask you to lead their picket line. Their slogan is 'Fewer headbutts, please.' A company of skeletons arrives to take their jobs.
text.c: The goblins have a picket line and a promising rhyme for 'dental'. The dark lord has hired skeletons, who insist they have no interest in teeth.
text.x: The strikebreakers are skeletons. The goblins ask you to explain that having no teeth is not a good bloody reason to oppose dental care.

choices.label: Lead the strike chant
choices.win: The chanting draws a crowd. The dark lord comes out to negotiate.
choices.lose: You forget the words. The guards break up the chanting with their shields.

onWin.memory: The chanting draws a crowd. The dark lord comes out to negotiate.

choices.label: Invite the skeletons to join the strike
choices.win: You point out that skeletons need bone repairs. They join the goblins.
choices.lose: The skeletons refuse and push through the picket line, taking you with them.

onWin.memory: You point out that skeletons need bone repairs. They join the goblins.

text.f: The goblins' wages come from an enchanted purse. It screams whenever anyone claims overtime. The dark lord calls this an accounting feature.
text.c: The payroll purse screams every time a goblin earns overtime. The dark lord says it is working as intended. The goblins disagree.
text.x: The enchanted payroll purse screams at every overtime claim. The dark lord paid extra for that feature, the miserable bastard.

choices.label: Check the overtime figures
choices.win: You prove the purse has been rejecting valid claims. The dark lord must settle the arrears.
choices.lose: The purse mistakes your hand for a withdrawal request and bites it.

onWin.memory: You prove the purse has been rejecting valid claims. The dark lord must settle the arrears.

choices.label: Explain the pay rules to the purse
choices.win: The purse accepts the rules and starts paying the goblins. It still sighs between coins.
choices.lose: The purse refuses to listen and snaps shut on your fingers.

onWin.memory: The purse accepts the rules and starts paying the goblins. It still sighs between coins.

finaleChoices.label: Present the workers' signed collective agreement

win.f: Dental cover, lunch breaks, no unpaid hauntings. The dark lord signs in washable ink.

v.gritty: Dental cover, lunch breaks, no unpaid hauntings. The dark lord signs in washable blood.
v.brutal: Dental cover, lunch breaks, no unpaid hauntings. The dark lord presses a bleeding thumb to the agreement.

finaleChoices.lose: He signs, then disputes the lunch definition. Lawyers arrive.

onWin.memory: You won the goblins a signed collective agreement.

text.f: The hellhound's three heads want three different walks. One wants the park, one wants the butcher's, and one has spotted a squirrel. You have one lead.
text.c: Two hellhound heads agree on the park. The third has voted for a squirrel and considers the debate closed. The lead is getting very tight.
text.x: Two heads want the park. The third has seen a squirrel and is dragging you towards it. Nobody mentioned that the bloody lead was fireproof for a reason.

choices.label: Persuade all three heads to take the park route
choices.win: You promise a stop at the butcher’s on the way back. All three heads follow you.
choices.lose: The third head spots another squirrel and drags you through a hedge.

onWin.memory: You promise a stop at the butcher’s on the way back. All three heads follow you.

choices.label: Buy one sausage for each head
choices.win: All three heads chew happily while you regain control of the lead.
choices.lose: The butcher refuses to sell any more sausages.

onWin.memory: All three heads chew happily while you regain control of the lead.

choices.label: Hold on when the squirrel runs
choices.win: You brace yourself and keep the hound on the path. The squirrel escapes.
choices.lose: The hound drags you across the park. You arrive well before the lead stops moving.

onWin.memory: You brace yourself and keep the hound on the path. The squirrel escapes.

onLose.memory: The hound drags you across the park. You arrive well before the lead stops moving.

text.f: The book says it was returned on time three hundred years ago. The librarian says her records disagree. A faded receipt is stuck inside the cover.
text.c: The library wants three hundred years of late fees. The book claims it was returned on time and asks whether anybody has bothered to read its receipt.
text.x: The librarian wants three hundred years of late fees. The book says the receipt is inside its cover. Apparently nobody has opened the bloody thing.

choices.label: Read the faded return receipt
choices.win: You recover the date and request a hearing to challenge the fine.
choices.lose: You misread the ink. The librarian slams a reference volume onto your fingers.

onWin.memory: You recover the date and request a hearing to challenge the fine.

choices.label: Pay for a backdated renewal
choices.win: The library renews the book from its original due date. The receipt will help with the final return.
choices.lose: The librarian refuses the renewal.

onWin.memory: The library renews the book from its original due date. The receipt will help with the final return.

choices.label: Carry the book through the returns gate
choices.win: You get the book inside before the librarian can object.
choices.lose: The book snaps shut on your hand as the returns gate closes.

onWin.memory: You get the book inside before the librarian can object.

text.f: A committee of talking dictionaries reviews the receipt. The librarian argues that 'returned' did not mean the same thing three hundred years ago.
text.c: The dictionary committee is examining your receipt. The librarian is trying to redefine 'returned'. Even the thesaurus thinks this is a stretch.
text.x: The librarian claims the word 'returned' has changed meaning. The dictionary committee has heard some pedantic bullshit, but this is new.

choices.label: Compare the receipt with the old definition
choices.win: The committee rules that the book was returned. It issues a written decision.
choices.lose: You cite the wrong edition. A dictionary drops heavily onto your foot.

onWin.memory: The committee rules that the book was returned. It issues a written decision.

choices.label: Ask the children’s librarian to explain it
choices.win: She gives a very clear explanation. The committee rules in your favor.
choices.lose: She explains the overdue-book rules slowly, using you as the bad example.

onWin.memory: She gives a very clear explanation. The committee rules in your favor.

text.f: The returns chute jams. The book is stuck behind a shelf in Reference. The librarian says you may fetch it, provided you do so in complete silence.
text.c: The returns chute has lodged the book behind Reference. The librarian offers access, then points to a sign forbidding noise, ladders and useful assistance.
text.x: The book is stuck behind Reference. The librarian forbids noise, ladders and moving the shelves. Getting it back will apparently require a bloody miracle.

choices.label: Find the service hatch in the catalog
choices.win: The maintenance plan shows a hatch behind the shelf. You recover the book quietly.
choices.lose: You pull the wrong shelf latch. A stack of atlases falls on you.

onWin.memory: The maintenance plan shows a hatch behind the shelf. You recover the book quietly.

choices.label: Crawl under the shelves
choices.win: You squeeze under the shelves and recover the book without a sound.
choices.lose: You sneeze in the dust. The librarian drags you out by your ankles.

onWin.memory: You squeeze under the shelves and recover the book without a sound.

finaleChoices.label: Present the dictionary committee’s ruling
finaleChoices.win: The librarian accepts the ruling and cancels the fine. The book requests a quieter shelf.
finaleChoices.lose: The librarian finds a missing signature. She drops the appeals ledger onto your foot.

onWin.memory: The librarian accepts the ruling and cancels the fine. The book requests a quieter shelf.

text.f: The giant's wardrobe kit has six identical panels and no labels. The instructions show a smiling person holding a single tiny key. The giant is not smiling.
text.c: The instructions promise easy assembly. They show a tiny smiling person, but omit the part where the screws weigh as much as you do.
text.x: Six unlabelled panels, screws the size of goats and one tiny key. The instructions say this takes twenty minutes. Absolute bollocks.

choices.label: Work out which panel is the door
choices.win: You identify the hinges. The giant is delighted that the wardrobe might eventually open.
choices.lose: You fit the door as the floor. The giant asks you to demonstrate it.

onWin.memory: You identify the hinges. The giant is delighted that the wardrobe might eventually open.

choices.label: Hire a goblin assembly crew
choices.win: The goblins label the panels and put up a sturdy frame.
choices.lose: The assembly crew declines the booking.

onWin.memory: The goblins label the panels and put up a sturdy frame.

choices.label: Force the panels into place
choices.win: The joints fit after one determined shove. You discreetly pocket the splinters.
choices.lose: A panel slips from its groove and knocks you down.

onLose.memory: A panel slips from its groove and knocks you down.

text.f: The wardrobe stands upright, but one enormous screw remains. Whenever the giant opens a door, the whole frame leans towards you.
text.c: One screw left. The giant says that usually means a spare. The wardrobe leans ominously towards the side without a hinge.
text.x: The giant calls the last screw a spare. The wardrobe is leaning at a frankly alarming angle. You would prefer not to test that theory from underneath it.

choices.label: Find the empty hole in the hinge
choices.win: You fit the missing screw. The wardrobe stops leaning.
choices.lose: You loosen the wrong hinge. The door swings into your face.

onWin.memory: You fit the missing screw. The wardrobe stops leaning.

choices.label: Brace the frame during a load test
choices.win: You hold the frame steady while the giant secures the hinge.
choices.lose: The giant hangs up his coat. You discover how much a giant’s coat weighs.

onWin.memory: You hold the frame steady while the giant secures the hinge.

text.f: The dark lord's nephew demands the moon as a bedtime snack. He has a summoning wand and has already moved it worryingly close to the window.
text.c: The nephew wants to eat the moon. With an ordinary child this would be a negotiation. This one has a wand and a telescope.
text.x: The nephew wants the moon for supper and has a summoning wand. You need to get the little sod into bed before he ruins the tides.

choices.label: Tell a story about a moon-eating stomach ache
choices.win: The nephew decides the moon can stay where it is. For now, he asks for toast.
choices.lose: He wants to see whether your story is true. The wand fires past your ear.

onWin.memory: The nephew decides the moon can stay where it is. For now, he asks for toast.

choices.label: Offer a cheese wheel instead
choices.win: He accepts the cheese as a practice moon and puts down the wand.
choices.lose: He throws the cheese back. It was a disappointingly accurate moon.

onWin.memory: He accepts the cheese as a practice moon and puts down the wand.

choices.label: Buy a licensed sleep spell
choices.win: The sleep spell settles him down long enough for a bedtime story.
choices.lose: The spell seller has none left.

onWin.memory: The sleep spell settles him down long enough for a bedtime story.

text.f: The nephew's pet monster, Gerald, refuses to go under the bed. The child has been asking it to check for monsters. Gerald is beginning to worry.
text.c: Gerald is supposed to be the monster under the bed. The nephew has asked him to check beneath it first. Gerald would like a second opinion.
text.x: Gerald refuses to go under the bed until someone checks it for monsters. The child has managed to frighten his own bloody monster.

choices.label: Reassure Gerald after checking the room
choices.win: Gerald settles under the bed. The child agrees it is safe to put his feet down.
choices.lose: Gerald mistakes your reassuring shadow for another monster and knocks you over.

onWin.memory: Gerald settles under the bed. The child agrees it is safe to put his feet down.

choices.label: Take the first shift under the bed
choices.win: You check the dust and give the all-clear. Gerald takes over gratefully.
choices.lose: You bang your head on the bed frame. The nephew rates your growl disappointingly low.

onWin.memory: You check the dust and give the all-clear. Gerald takes over gratefully.

text.f: The tower asks for the name of the wizard's first familiar. He remembers it was a snail. He has forgotten the name. The snail lives just down the path.
text.c: The wizard remembers his first familiar was a snail. The tower requires its name. The snail is nearby and is taking a very long time to introduce itself.
text.x: The wizard has forgotten his familiar's name. It was a snail. He kept it for eighty years, the forgetful bastard.

choices.label: Find the snail’s old registration form
choices.win: The familiar register lists the snail’s name. The tower sends a recovery code.
choices.lose: The register collapses from its shelf. You are briefly buried in familiar paperwork.

onWin.memory: The familiar register lists the snail’s name. The tower sends a recovery code.

choices.label: Pay the helpdesk gargoyle
choices.win: The gargoyle retrieves the familiar’s name and starts the recovery process.
choices.lose: The gargoyle refuses the request.

onWin.memory: The gargoyle retrieves the familiar’s name and starts the recovery process.

choices.label: Climb to the wizard’s window
choices.win: You bypass the locked door and find his recovery notes on the desk.
choices.lose: The window has the same lock. You lose your grip while arguing with it.

onLose.memory: The window has the same lock. You lose your grip while arguing with it.

text.f: The tower has posted a recovery code to the snail. The code expires at sunset. The snail is still crossing the doorstep to collect it.
text.c: The recovery code has arrived. Unfortunately, the snail insists on opening its own post. The code expires at sunset, which it considers rather hasty.
text.x: The code expires at sunset. The snail insists on opening its own post and is still crossing the doorstep. You may be here all bloody day.

choices.label: Read the code over the snail’s shoulder
choices.win: You read all six digits before the code expires.
choices.lose: The snail turns to block your view. You lean too far and fall off the doorstep.

onWin.memory: You read all six digits before the code expires.

choices.label: Ask the tower to extend the deadline
choices.win: The tower allows extra time for snail post. You receive a valid code.
choices.lose: The tower refuses the extension and shocks you for repeated requests.

onWin.memory: The tower allows extra time for snail post. You receive a valid code.

text.f: Too many wrong guesses have locked the door. To try again, you must identify every tower in a set of pictures. The wizard calls several of them 'large sheds'.
text.c: The door's security test asks you to identify towers. The wizard is disputing the difference between a tower and a tall shed. The door is counting failures.
text.x: The wizard keeps calling towers 'tall sheds'. The door's security test keeps rejecting him. You need to settle this before another bloody lockout.

choices.label: Identify the towers correctly
choices.win: You complete the test. The door grants another password attempt.
choices.lose: You select a windmill. The door’s alarm knocks you off the step.

onWin.memory: You complete the test. The door grants another password attempt.

choices.label: Persuade the wizard to stop helping
choices.win: The wizard steps aside. You finish the test without his architectural opinions.
choices.lose: He shouts another answer over yours. The door rejects both and slams shut.

onWin.memory: The wizard steps aside. You finish the test without his architectural opinions.

text.f: Someone has put the bride's ex beside the garlic dip. The groom says it was an accident. The ex has already asked for a different table.
text.c: The bride's ex is seated beside the garlic dip. The groom insists this was an innocent mistake. He is having trouble suppressing a smile.
text.x: The groom has seated the bride's ex beside the garlic dip. He calls it a mistake. The smug bastard has also put garlic on the place card.

choices.label: Rearrange the seating plan
choices.win: You separate the ex, the groom and the garlic. Dinner can begin.
choices.lose: You move the ex beside another former spouse. Their argument sends a chair your way.

onWin.memory: You separate the ex, the groom and the garlic. Dinner can begin.

choices.label: Pay to replace the garlic dip
choices.win: A waiter replaces the dip with beetroot. The ex agrees to stay.
choices.lose: The caterer refuses the replacement order.

onWin.memory: A waiter replaces the dip with beetroot. The ex agrees to stay.

choices.label: Carry the garlic outside
choices.win: You remove the garlic before anyone starts a fight.
choices.lose: You spill garlic dip down your front. Several guests shove you toward the exit.

onLose.memory: You spill garlic dip down your front. Several guests shove you toward the exit.

text.f: The best man starts a slideshow of the bride's previous weddings. There are forty-seven. The groom asks how to turn the projector off.
text.c: The best man's toast includes forty-seven previous husbands and a slideshow. The bride has stopped smiling. The groom is looking for the plug.
text.x: The best man has brought slides of all forty-seven previous husbands. The bride wants the projector off before the bloody engagement ends.

choices.label: Pull the projector cable discreetly
choices.win: The screen goes dark. The bride calls it a welcome technical fault.
choices.lose: You pull a guest’s tail instead. The slides continue while the guest pursues you.

onWin.memory: The screen goes dark. The bride calls it a welcome technical fault.

choices.label: Offer a short toast to the newlyweds
choices.win: Your toast wins the room. The best man reluctantly puts away the slides.
choices.lose: You begin with “until death do you part.” The vampires are not impressed.

onWin.memory: Your toast wins the room. The best man reluctantly puts away the slides.

text.f: A splash from the Fountain of Youth has turned the plumber into a child. He remembers the repair, but cannot reach the valve. His drawing might help.
text.c: The plumber is now six and cannot reach his tools. He has drawn the broken valve in crayon. His employer is disputing the call-out fee.
text.x: The plumber is six years old and his boss still expects him to finish the bloody repair. He has drawn you a diagram in crayon.

choices.label: Read the plumber’s crayon diagram
choices.win: You identify the leaking valve and shut it off. The plumber gives you a gold star.
choices.lose: You open the wrong valve. A jet of water knocks you into the tool chest.

onWin.memory: You identify the leaking valve and shut it off. The plumber gives you a gold star.

choices.label: Hire a plumber who has not been splashed
choices.win: A second plumber arrives with a ladder and seals the leak.
choices.lose: No other plumber will take the job.

onWin.memory: A second plumber arrives with a ladder and seals the leak.

choices.label: Hold the pipe closed for the plumber
choices.win: You stop the spray while he tightens the valve.
choices.lose: The pipe slips from your grip and sprays you across the courtyard.

onLose.memory: The pipe slips from your grip and sprays you across the courtyard.

text.f: The fountain is clogged with old birthday candles. Water is spilling across the courtyard, making everyone who steps in it younger. A toddler demands his pension.
text.c: Old birthday candles have blocked the fountain. The flooded courtyard is getting younger by the minute. A toddler is complaining about his pension.
text.x: Birthday candles have blocked the fountain. The flooded courtyard is full of furious toddlers demanding their pensions. Somebody needs to clear the bloody drain.

choices.label: Remove the candles with the drain hook
choices.win: The candles come free and the courtyard drains. The pensioners demand dry socks.
choices.lose: The hook slips. A spray of water sends you sprawling across the paving stones.

onWin.memory: The candles come free and the courtyard drains. The pensioners demand dry socks.

choices.label: Wade in and reach the overflow valve
choices.win: You open the valve before the water rises any farther.
choices.lose: The water makes your boots too big. You trip before reaching the valve.

onWin.memory: You open the valve before the water rises any farther.

text.f: Two farmers are competing for the prize squash. One quietly offers you a smaller squash stuffed with coins. The other has brought a very large pitchfork.
text.c: One farmer offers you a squash full of coins. He calls it a free sample. His rival is watching your pockets with considerable interest.
text.x: One farmer offers you a squash stuffed with coins. His rival is watching with a pitchfork. These bastards take the vegetable contest seriously.

choices.label: Question both farmers in public
choices.win: Both farmers explain their methods. With witnesses watching, neither can offer another bribe.
choices.lose: One farmer accuses you of favoritism. The crowd pushes you off the judging platform.

onWin.memory: Both farmers explain their methods. With witnesses watching, neither can offer another bribe.

choices.label: Buy the coin-filled squash as evidence
choices.win: You keep the coins as evidence and disqualify the farmer who offered them.
choices.lose: The farmer withdraws his offer.

onWin.memory: You keep the coins as evidence and disqualify the farmer who offered them.

choices.label: Lift the giant squash onto the scales
choices.win: You get an honest weight. The farmer who exaggerated his entry goes very quiet.
choices.lose: The squash slips off the scales and pins your foot.

onLose.memory: The squash slips off the scales and pins your foot.

text.f: Your kraken student has booked a private swimming lesson. It is clinging to the pier and insists the water looks deeper from this close up.
text.c: The kraken is clinging to the pier. It has eight armbands, but would prefer a ninth in case one of its arms gets nervous.
text.x: The kraken has eight armbands and still will not let go of the pier. It says the water looks bloody deep. You can see the bottom.

choices.label: Fit the armbands one at a time
choices.win: The kraken relaxes as you check each armband. It agrees to try the shallow water.
choices.lose: You tighten a strap too far. The startled kraken knocks you off the pier.

onWin.memory: The kraken relaxes as you check each armband. It agrees to try the shallow water.

choices.label: Pay to keep spectators off the pier
choices.win: The lifeguard clears the pier. The kraken agrees to practice in private.
choices.lose: The lifeguard refuses to close the pier.

onWin.memory: The lifeguard clears the pier. The kraken agrees to practice in private.

choices.label: Demonstrate how to float
choices.win: You float calmly beside the pier. The kraken loosens its grip to watch.
choices.lose: You swallow a mouthful of water. The kraken hauls you out and loses confidence.

onWin.memory: You float calmly beside the pier. The kraken loosens its grip to watch.

text.f: Other krakens arrive to watch. Your student hides behind a pool noodle. Most of it remains visible, but you decide not to mention that.
text.c: Your student tries to hide behind one pool noodle as other krakens arrive. It is a heroic effort to conceal something larger than the pier.
text.x: The kraken is hiding behind a pool noodle. The other krakens can plainly see it, but you would rather not make the poor sod feel worse.

choices.label: Ask the onlookers to encourage it
choices.win: The other krakens admit they were nervous beginners too. Your student comes out from behind the noodle.
choices.lose: The cheering creates a wave that sweeps you across the pier.

onWin.memory: The other krakens admit they were nervous beginners too. Your student comes out from behind the noodle.

choices.label: Practice beside the noodle until it relaxes
choices.win: The kraken stops watching the crowd and starts copying your strokes.
choices.lose: The kraken grabs you for reassurance. Eight arms are considerably more reassurance than you need.

onWin.memory: The kraken stops watching the crowd and starts copying your strokes.

finaleChoices.label: Use the private lesson’s floating routine
finaleChoices.win: The kraken lets go, floats, and begins to swim. It asks you to watch one more length.
finaleChoices.lose: Eight arms choose eight directions. You are the meeting point.

onWin.memory: The kraken lets go, floats, and begins to swim. It asks you to watch one more length.

text.f: The snail parade has stopped at its first curb. The marshal has scheduled a six-hour climb. The finish line is only across the street.
text.c: The first curb has stopped the snail parade. The marshal allows six hours for the climb. The band has already played its entire song twice.
text.x: The snail parade has stopped at a curb. The marshal says climbing it will take six hours. You could have carried the whole bloody parade across by now.

choices.label: Find a route around the curb
choices.win: You lead the parade down a ramp. The marshal records this as a major expedition.
choices.lose: The ramp ends beside a salt merchant’s stall. You slip while steering the parade away.

onWin.memory: You lead the parade down a ramp. The marshal records this as a major expedition.

choices.label: Hire a tiny wagon
choices.win: You lift the snails over the curb in a wagon. They insist it still counts as marching.
choices.lose: The wagon rental is closed.

onWin.memory: You lift the snails over the curb in a wagon. They insist it still counts as marching.

choices.label: Carry the marshal to lead the way
choices.win: You lift the marshal onto the sidewalk. The parade follows his flag up a safer slope.
choices.lose: His ceremonial shell is heavier than it looks. You fall backward into the gutter.

onWin.memory: You lift the marshal onto the sidewalk. The parade follows his flag up a safer slope.

text.f: Rain has flooded the parade route. The snails love the weather, but the marshal refuses to change course because the programs have already been printed.
text.c: The parade route is underwater. The snails are delighted. The marshal says a detour is impossible because he has personally laminated the map.
text.x: The street is flooded. The snails love it. The marshal refuses a detour because he has already printed the bloody programs.

choices.label: Persuade the marshal to approve a detour
choices.win: He approves a dry route and announces that the change was his idea.
choices.lose: He orders the original route. You slip into the flooded gutter while arguing with him.

onWin.memory: He approves a dry route and announces that the change was his idea.

choices.label: Build a bridge with your umbrella
choices.win: The snails cross the umbrella in single file. The marshal requests a ribbon-cutting ceremony.
choices.lose: The umbrella folds under the wet shells. You fall into the gutter trying to hold it open.

onWin.memory: The snails cross the umbrella in single file. The marshal requests a ribbon-cutting ceremony.

text.f: Your rival is rehearsing a victory speech into a hairbrush. The trophy engraver has left the winner's name blank. Your rival has asked him to reconsider.
text.c: Your rival is practicing a victory speech. The engraver refuses to add a name until the contest ends. Neither of them is enjoying the conversation.
text.x: Your rival wants the trophy engraved before the contest. The engraver says no. The arrogant bastard has offered to spell the name out more slowly.

choices.label: Honor your truce with the rival
choices.win: You agree to ask the Guild for a shared award. Your rival puts away the speech.
choices.lose: Your rival refuses to discuss the truce.

onWin.memory: You agree to ask the Guild for a shared award. Your rival puts away the speech.

choices.label: Check the contest rules
choices.win: You find the rule requiring an unmarked trophy. The engraver thanks you.
choices.lose: You mistake a sponsor’s advertisement for the rules. Your rival gives you a very public shove.

onWin.memory: You find the rule requiring an unmarked trophy. The engraver thanks you.

choices.label: Lift the podium during the warm-up
choices.win: Your display makes the rival stop rehearsing and start paying attention.
choices.lose: The podium is bolted down. Your attempted warm-up ends with a strained back.

onWin.memory: Your display makes the rival stop rehearsing and start paying attention.

onLose.memory: The podium is bolted down. Your attempted warm-up ends with a strained back.

text.f: You and your rival want to share the award. The Guild wants to know who will do the work. The engraver wants to know whose name goes first.
text.c: The Guild will consider a shared award if you agree on the work. The engraver has suggested alphabetical order. Your rival suddenly wants a different name.
text.x: You have agreed to share the award. Now the Guild wants twice the work for one salary. Those greedy bastards have moved quickly.

choices.label: Negotiate a joint hero contract
choices.win: The Guild agrees to split the duties and pay both heroes. The engraver adds an ampersand.
choices.lose: The Guild offers one salary. Your rival kicks the chair out as negotiations collapse.

onWin.memory: The Guild agrees to split the duties and pay both heroes. The engraver adds an ampersand.

choices.label: Get both names on the agreement
choices.win: You both sign a fair division of the work. The Guild accepts the agreement.
choices.lose: Your rival signs the wrong page. A clerk ejects you for tampering with the paperwork.

onWin.memory: You both sign a fair division of the work. The Guild accepts the agreement.

text.f: The Guild has invited former clients to describe your work. Your rival has paid actors to join the line. Several are still holding their scripts.
text.c: Your rival has hired actors to criticize you. They are easy to spot: your actual clients rarely carry scripts with stage directions.
text.x: The rival has paid actors to complain about your work. The lazy bastards are still reading from their scripts in the witness line.

choices.label: Ask your actual clients to speak
choices.win: Their accounts are unpolished, but the details convince the Guild.
choices.lose: One client remembers only the damage. The audience starts throwing programs.

onWin.memory: Their accounts are unpolished, but the details convince the Guild.

choices.label: Expose the actors in the witness line
choices.win: You collect three identical scripts. The Guild removes the actors.
choices.lose: You accuse a real client by mistake. They push you off the witness platform.

onWin.memory: You collect three identical scripts. The Guild removes the actors.

finaleChoices.label: Offer the shared hero contract
finaleChoices.win: The Guild accepts. Two heroes, one trophy, absolutely incompatible office hours.
finaleChoices.lose: The Guild demands a probationary duel. Human resources are terrible.

onWin.memory: You and your rival became joint Heroes of the Year.

text.f: Your rival has blocked the road to pose for a heroic painting. The artist asks you to stand beside them and look as though you needed rescuing.
text.c: Your rival wants a painting of a spontaneous rescue. They have booked the artist, blocked the road and assigned you the role of grateful victim.
text.x: Your rival has blocked the road for a painting of a heroic rescue. The vain bastard wants you to pose as the helpless victim.

choices.label: Charge a fee for posing
choices.win: The artist agrees to pay you. Your rival objects to the expense but keeps the pose.
choices.lose: Your rival insists you are the villain and demonstrates the rescue by shoving you aside.

onWin.memory: The artist agrees to pay you. Your rival objects to the expense but keeps the pose.

choices.label: Pay for a quiet truce
choices.win: You agree to stop sabotaging each other. Your rival quietly admits the competition is exhausting.
choices.lose: Your rival declines the discussion.

onWin.memory: You agree to stop sabotaging each other. Your rival quietly admits the competition is exhausting.

choices.label: Slip behind the artist’s canvas
choices.win: You get past while the rival holds a heroic pose for an empty road.
choices.lose: You trip over the easel. The artist blames you for ruining the composition.

onWin.memory: You get past while the rival holds a heroic pose for an empty road.

text.f: You find your rival sitting beside the road, unable to open a lunch tin. They ask whether you have a knife, then remember you are competitors.
text.c: Your rival has defeated monsters all week and is now losing a fight with a lunch-tin clip. They ask you not to tell the sponsors.
text.x: Your rival cannot open a lunch tin. All that swagger, and a fucking clip has stopped the victory tour.

choices.label: Open it and promise not to tell
choices.win: You open the tin. Over lunch, you agree to stop making the contest personal.
choices.lose: The clip snaps on your fingers. Neither of you mentions the failed rescue.

onWin.memory: You open the tin. Over lunch, you agree to stop making the contest personal.

choices.label: Buy lunch for both of you
choices.win: You share two pies and agree to compete without sabotaging each other.
choices.lose: The pie shop is closed.

onWin.memory: You share two pies and agree to compete without sabotaging each other.

choices.label: Force the lid open
choices.win: The lid flies off. So does most of the soup. Your rival thanks you very carefully.
choices.lose: The tin slips and hits your knee. Your rival offers extremely unhelpful advice.

onWin.memory: The lid flies off. So does most of the soup. Your rival thanks you very carefully.

text.f: Your rival has a spare invitation to the trophy ceremony. They ask whether you would like to come, then add that a proper nemesis should really be there.
text.c: Your rival offers you an invitation. They say the ceremony requires a formidable nemesis. It appears to be an awkward way of asking you to come along.
text.x: Your rival wants you at the ceremony but cannot simply ask. The poor bastard has spent all year practicing threats instead of conversation.

choices.label: Accept the invitation politely
choices.win: Your rival smiles. You agree to keep the final contest fair.
choices.lose: You both speak at once, each mistaking the other’s politeness for a threat. A shove ends the conversation.

onWin.memory: Your rival smiles. You agree to keep the final contest fair.

choices.label: Check the invitation’s small print
choices.win: The only extra rule is to wear shoes. You confirm your invitation is valid.
choices.lose: You unfold the card too close to the rival’s face. They swat it, and your nose, aside.

onWin.memory: The only extra rule is to wear shoes. You confirm your invitation is valid.

choices.label: Keep the invitation inside your boot
choices.win: The invitation is safe. You may need to air it out before the ceremony.
choices.lose: You lose your balance while removing the boot. The invitation lands in a puddle.

onWin.memory: The invitation is safe. You may need to air it out before the ceremony.
